name: Peter Thiel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Peter Thiel returns to the Midas List for a 16th time as the cofounder and general partner of venture fund Founders Fund.

Among its investments are Stripe and SpaceX, two of the most valuable unicorns in the world; Stripe was valued at $159 billion as of February 2026; SpaceX is planning to go public this summer at a valuation of $1.75 trillion.
He also cofounded CIA-backed big data startup Palantir, which went public via a direct listing in 2020.
Thiel, the first big investor in Facebook, has sold most of his stake in the social network; He left the board in 2022.
His Thiel Foundation gives a small number of young entrepreneurs $100,000 over two years to skip college and build their own company.
Thiel moved to Los Angeles from San Francisco in early 2018 after calling Silicon Valley a "one-party state."
forbes_facts: Thiel found himself at the center of controversy after Forbes revealed in May 2016 that he was secretly funding lawsuits in an attempt to destroy Gawker Media.
Thiel, a Trump delegate in California, was one of the first outspoken Trump supporters in Silicon Valley in 2016.

name: Ray Dalio
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Ray Dalio is the founder of the world's biggest hedge fund firm, Bridgewater Associates, which now manages $92 billion.
Dalio stepped down as CEO in 2017, retired as co-CIO in 2022 and sold off his full stake in the firm by 2025.
Dalio grew up in a middle-class Long Island neighborhood and started playing the markets at age 12, getting tips from golfers for whom he caddied.
In 1975, after earning an MBA from Harvard Business School, he launched Bridgewater from his two-bedroom New York City apartment.
Dalio has given more than $1 billion to philanthropic causes. His Dalio Philanthropies has supported microfinance and public education.
forbes_facts: In 2017, Dalio published "Principles: Life & Work," a New York Times bestseller that codifies his principles.
Bridgewater is known for its culture of "radical transparency," including encouraging dissent, openly airing disagreements and recording all meetings.

name: Anthoni Salim
forbes_bio: Anthoni Salim heads the Salim Group, with investments in food, retail, banking, telecom and energy.
He is the CEO of Indofood, one of the world's largest makers of instant noodles.
Anthoni is the youngest of three sons of the late Liem Sioe Liong, a tycoon who for decades was very close to president Suharto.
The Salims own a stake in Hong Kong-listed investment firm First Pacific, which has interests in Indofood and telecom firm PLDT of the Philippines.
He also owns stakes in mining companies such as Bumi Resources, Medco Energi and Amman Mineral.

name: Rodolphe Saadé
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Rodolphe Saadé is the son of late shipping magnate Jacques Saadé, who died in 2018.
Jacques founded CMA CGM, now one of the world's largest shipping companies, in Marseille, France in 1978.
Rodolphe jointly controls the company with his siblings, Tanya Saadé Zeenny and Jacques Saadé Jr., as well as his mother Naila.
He took over from his father as chairman of the board and CEO of CMA CGM Group in 2017.
The $55.5 billion (2024 revenues) company operates more than 700 vessels, serving 420 commercial ports in 160 countries.

name: Ding Shijia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ding Shijia is the deputy chairman of Anta Sports, one of China's largest homegrown sportswear brands.
It sells under a range of brands such as Anta, Fila, Descente and Kolon Sport.
In 2019 the company led a consortium to acquire Finnish group Amer Sports, with brands including Arc'teryx, Wilson and Salomon, at $5.2 billion.
Amer Sports went public on the New York Stock Exchange in February 2024, raising $1.4 billion.
Ding's younger brother Ding Shizhong, Anta's chairman, is also a billionaire.

name: H. Fisk Johnson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014)
forbes_bio: H. Fisk Johnson III is the chairman and CEO of SC Johnson, a privately-held cleaning products company.
He is the fifth generation of the Johnson family to lead the company.
The company, which has $11.4 billion in estimated revenues, is best known for brands like Windex, Off! and Pledge.
Fisk and his three siblings are all shareholders of SC Johnson. Together they own a majority of the company.
Fisk's late father, Sam Johnson Jr. (d. 2004), ran SC Johnson from 1966 to 2000.
forbes_facts: H. Fisk received 4 degrees from Cornell University: a bachelor's, a master's in engineering, an M.B.A and a Ph.D.
In January 2017 H. Fisk and his siblings pledged $150 million to found the SC Johnson College of Business at Cornell University.

name: Abdulla bin Ahmad Al Ghurair
forbes_bio: Abdulla bin Ahmad Al Ghurair founded Mashreqbank, a leading U.A.E. bank, in 1967. He stepped down as chairman in 2019.
His eponymous holding company has interests in food, construction and real estate; non-family members are part of the leadership team.
His construction company did the exterior cladding of Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, and helped build the Dubai Metro.
His brother Saif Al Ghurair, who passed away in 2019, was also a billionaire.
forbes_facts: In 2015, Al Ghurair pledged one third of his group's assets to a foundation that invests in education programs in the U.A.E.
His foundation aims to help 15,000 Arab students get a secondary and university education by 2025 by providing scholarships.

name: James Chambers
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: James Cox Chambers inherited an estimated 17% stake in communications, media and automotive conglomerate Cox Enterprises from his mother Anne Cox Chambers.
His grandfather, James M. Cox, founded what became Cox Enterprises in 1898.
Both his sisters, Katharine Rayner and Margaretta Taylor, also inherited an estimated 17% stake each in Cox Enterprises.
Neither James nor his sisters or mother have ever had an active role in the company.
His cousin, Jim Kennedy, is chairman emeritus of Cox Enterprises. His nephew, Alex Taylor, is CEO and chairman.
forbes_facts: James Chambers is a Bard College trustee and alum.
He owns a minority stake in the NBA's Atlanta Hawks.

name: Sanjit Biswas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2022); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2021)
forbes_bio: In 2015, Sanjit Biswas and John Bicket cofounded Samsara, a platform that uses AI-powered tools to help companies, such as transportation and construction businesses, increase efficiency and improve safety.
Biswas serves as CEO of Samsara, which is based in San Francisco; the company listed its shares on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021.
Samsara operates in North America, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region; it has more than 20,000 customers.
Biswas and Bicket met at MIT as graduate students.
Before Samsara, the pair cofounded the cloud networking company Meraki, which they sold to Cisco in 2012 for $1.2 billion.

name: Norman Braman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Norman Braman owns one of Florida's largest car dealerships, Braman Motorcars, which has more than $3 billion in annual revenue.
Braman made his first fortune selling pharmaceuticals and cosmetics.
Born in Philadelphia to immigrant parents, he was a water boy for the Eagles, the NFL team he bought in 1985 and sold in 1994 for a $120 million profit.
An avid art collector, he helped bring the prestigious Swiss art fair, Art Basel, to Miami in 2002.
He and his wife funded the construction of Miami's Institute for Contemporary Art, a free museum which opened in 2017.
forbes_facts: In college, Braman worked at a retail store in downtown Philadelphia where he says he earned 50 cents an hour.
In 2025, Miami Beach renamed a portion of 17th Street "Norman Braman Way" to honor his contributions to the city.
